test_cases.test_name: Workflow Configuration and Chain-of-Custody Verification
test_cases.objective: Verify the system's ability to configure and execute a standard workflow template while enforcing dual-scan chain-of-custody.
prerequisites: System fully installed and configured (GAMP Cat 4 baseline).
Test patient record created.
Two unique physical verification scanners configured and linked.

test_steps.action: Configure a new end-to-end workflow template incorporating Apheresis, Manufacturing Slotting, and QC Release steps (URS-028-001).
test_steps.expected_result: Workflow template is saved successfully and available for instantiation.

test_steps.action: Initiate a patient journey using the configured template and proceed to the first custody handoff point (e.g., Apheresis collection).
test_steps.expected_result: System prompts for dual-scan verification for the patient identifier and the collection container ID.

test_steps.action: Attempt to proceed past the custody handoff point using only one valid scan (e.g., only Patient ID scan).
test_steps.expected_result: System blocks progression and logs an audit event indicating failed custody verification (URS-028-002).

test_steps.action: Complete the dual-scan verification successfully for the custody transfer.
test_steps.expected_result: The custody event is recorded with accurate timestamps and user/device IDs in the audit trail (URS-028-008).

acceptance_criteria: The configured workflow executes correctly through the defined stages.
The system strictly enforces dual-scan verification for all defined custody handoffs.
All custody events are immutably recorded in the audit trail.
data_integrity_requirements: Custody records must be immutable.
Verification data (scans) must be captured accurately.

test_cases.test_name: Configurable Risk Scoring and E-Signature Validation
test_cases.objective: Validate the execution of configurable risk scoring rules and the enforcement of 21 CFR Part 11 compliant e-signatures for critical release actions.
prerequisites: System operational.
User accounts configured with appropriate e-signature privileges.
Risk scoring rule set configured to trigger a 'High Risk' flag based on specific input parameters (URS-028-005).

test_steps.action: Input test data into the workflow that is designed to trigger the pre-configured 'High Risk' scoring rule (e.g., simulated minor deviation data).
test_steps.expected_result: The system automatically calculates the risk score, and the workflow transitions to a 'Review Required' state, flagging the patient journey as High Risk (URS-028-005).

test_steps.action: Attempt to proceed from the QC Release step to the final Infusion step without applying an e-signature.
test_steps.expected_result: The system blocks the transition, displaying a message requiring authorization (URS-028-009).

test_steps.action: Apply a valid 21 CFR Part 11 compliant e-signature (Username/Password) to authorize the release of the High-Risk product.
test_steps.expected_result: The signature is validated, the workflow proceeds to Infusion, and the signature event is recorded with full audit details (URS-028-009).
data_to_capture: Audit trail entry confirming signature validation

test_steps.action: Review the audit trail for the QC Release step.
test_steps.expected_result: The audit trail clearly shows the risk score calculation, the block due to missing signature, and the successful signature event, including the reason for the signature (URS-028-008).
data_to_capture: Audit trail snippet showing all three events

acceptance_criteria: Configurable risk rules are correctly evaluated by the system.
Critical actions (like release) are blocked until a valid 21 CFR Part 11 e-signature is provided.
All signature events are fully traceable in the audit log.
data_integrity_requirements: E-signature integrity must be maintained.
Risk score calculation must be verifiable.

test_cases.test_name: Workflow Slot Allocation and Constraint Enforcement
test_cases.objective: Verify the system correctly allocates manufacturing slots based on configurable constraints and enforces scheduling rules.
prerequisites: System configured with at least two distinct workflow templates.
Manufacturing capacity constraints (e.g., maximum daily slots) defined.
Test patient records ready for scheduling.

test_steps.action: Initiate scheduling for Patient A, requiring a slot within the next 7 days, using Workflow Template 1.
test_steps.expected_result: The system successfully assigns a valid manufacturing slot within the defined constraints.

test_steps.action: Attempt to schedule Patient B, requiring a slot on a day where the maximum capacity constraint has already been met.
test_steps.expected_result: The system rejects the scheduling request for Patient B and provides an appropriate constraint violation message.
data_to_capture: Status of Patient B scheduling attempt

test_steps.action: Verify the audit trail records the successful scheduling of Patient A and the rejection of Patient B.
test_steps.expected_result: Audit trail entries exist for both actions, detailing the user/system initiating the request and the outcome.

acceptance_criteria: The system accurately allocates slots according to defined capacity limits.
Constraint violations result in clear rejection messages.
All scheduling actions are logged in the audit trail (URS-028-008).
data_integrity_requirements: Slot allocation data must be immutable once confirmed.

test_cases.test_name: Exception Handling for Cold Chain Excursion
test_cases.objective: Validate the system's ability to trigger and manage the exception workflow upon receiving a temperature excursion alert for a custody event.
prerequisites: System integrated with a simulated temperature monitoring service.
Exception handling workflow defined for temperature excursions (URS-028-004).
A custody event (e.g., shipment handover) is active for a test sample.

test_steps.action: Simulate a temperature excursion alert exceeding the defined threshold for the active custody event.
test_steps.expected_result: The system immediately flags the custody event as 'Excursion' and initiates the defined exception workflow.

test_steps.action: Verify that the system requires an authorized user to apply an e-signature to acknowledge and disposition the excursion event.
test_steps.expected_result: The system blocks further progression of the patient journey until the required e-signature is applied (URS-028-009).

test_steps.action: Review the GDP compliance records associated with the excursion event.
test_steps.expected_result: The system records the excursion details, the disposition decision, and the e-signature, meeting GDP documentation requirements (URS-028-010).

acceptance_criteria: Temperature excursions correctly trigger the defined exception workflow.
Critical disposition actions require 21 CFR Part 11 compliant e-signatures.
All excursion data is recorded accurately to support GDP compliance.
data_integrity_requirements: Excursion data must be tamper-proof.
E-signature data must meet Part 11 requirements.

test_cases.test_name: Verification of Custom Module Integration and Explainability
test_cases.objective: Validate the successful deployment, execution, and artifact generation of an optional custom algorithm module for patient-to-lot matching.
prerequisites: Custom algorithm module (e.g., matching optimizer) is containerized and deployed.
Test patient data requiring complex matching logic is available.
Integration points (APIs) for the custom module are configured.

test_steps.action: Initiate a patient journey requiring the custom matching algorithm via the orchestration platform.
test_steps.expected_result: The platform successfully calls the containerized custom module for processing.

test_steps.action: Review the output of the matching process to confirm the correct lot assignment based on the custom logic.
test_steps.expected_result: The assigned lot matches the expected outcome derived from the custom algorithm's defined rules.

test_steps.action: Retrieve and examine the explainability artifacts generated by the custom module for the decision made in Step 2.
test_steps.expected_result: A comprehensive artifact detailing the inputs, processing steps, and rationale leading to the matching decision is accessible and verifiable.

acceptance_criteria: The custom module executes without runtime errors.
The matching result aligns with the custom logic.
Explainability artifacts are generated and retained as required by URS-028-016.
data_integrity_requirements: Ensure the custom module output is correctly persisted in the audit trail.

test_cases.test_name: Verification of KPI Dashboard Accuracy and Audit Trail Completeness
test_cases.objective: Verify that key performance indicators (KPIs) displayed on the dashboard accurately reflect underlying system events and that the audit trail captures all custody handoffs.
prerequisites: At least five complete, end-to-end patient journeys (simulated or actual) have been processed.
System access to both the KPI dashboard and the raw audit log database.

test_steps.action: Calculate the total Vein-to-Vein (V2V) time for five distinct patient journeys by manually summing timestamps from the raw custody records (URS-028-002).
test_steps.expected_result: Five calculated V2V times are established for comparison.
data_to_capture: Manual V2V calculation results for 5 patients

test_steps.action: Access the KPI dashboard (URS-028-007) and record the displayed average and individual V2V times.
test_steps.expected_result: The dashboard displays metrics for the processed journeys.

test_steps.action: Compare the manually calculated V2V times (Step 1) against the dashboard metrics (Step 2) and verify that all custody events (e.g., dual-scan verification) are logged in the audit trail (URS-028-008).
test_steps.expected_result: Dashboard metrics match manual calculations within acceptable tolerance (e.g., < 1 second difference). All custody events are present in the audit trail.

acceptance_criteria: KPI dashboard accurately reflects the underlying data for V2V time.
The audit trail contains entries for every custody transfer and dual-scan verification event for the tested journeys.
data_integrity_requirements: Ensure data consistency between the operational database and the reporting layer.

test_cases.test_name: Verify GDP Compliance for Logistics Handoffs
test_cases.objective: To verify that the system correctly records and enforces GDP requirements during logistics handoffs, including temperature monitoring integration.
prerequisites: System configured with a logistics workflow template.
Simulated courier system integration active.
Test material prepared with temperature logging capability.

test_steps.action: Initiate a workflow requiring material shipment (e.g., from collection site to manufacturing).
test_steps.expected_result: The system generates a custody record requiring shipper ID and environmental monitoring data input.

test_steps.action: Simulate a temperature excursion event during transit via the integrated courier system interface.
test_steps.expected_result: The system flags the custody event as non-compliant, triggers URS-028-004 exception workflow, and prevents downstream processing until reviewed.

test_steps.action: Review the audit trail (URS-028-008) for the custody transfer and excursion event.
test_steps.expected_result: The audit trail accurately reflects the custody transfer, the simulated excursion data, and the initiation of the exception workflow.
data_to_capture: Audit trail entries for custody and excursion

acceptance_criteria: All logistics handoffs generate verifiable custody records.
Temperature excursion data is correctly ingested and triggers the defined exception workflow.
Audit trail integrity is maintained for all GDP-related events.
data_integrity_requirements: Environmental data must be immutable once recorded.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Concurrent Load Handling and Latency
test_cases.objective: To verify the system's ability to orchestrate 1,000 concurrent patient journeys while maintaining sub-second event processing latency.
prerequisites: Performance testing environment configured.
Load generation tools capable of simulating 1,000 concurrent workflows.
System baseline established.

test_steps.action: Initiate a load test simulating 1,000 concurrent, end-to-end patient workflows (URS-028-011).
test_steps.expected_result: All 1,000 workflows are successfully initiated and progress through the configured stages without failure.

test_steps.action: Monitor system performance metrics, specifically focusing on key event processing latency (e.g., custody scan confirmation, status updates).
test_steps.expected_result: The 95th percentile latency for critical workflow events remains below 1 second (URS-028-012).
data_to_capture: P95 latency metrics for key events

test_steps.action: Verify that the audit trail generation (URS-028-008) does not introduce significant bottlenecks during peak load.
test_steps.expected_result: Audit trail records are generated synchronously or asynchronously without causing workflow stalls exceeding the latency threshold.
data_to_capture: Audit log generation time stamps vs. event time stamps

acceptance_criteria: The system successfully manages 1,000 concurrent journeys.
Event processing latency meets the < 1 second requirement under normal load conditions.
No data loss or corruption occurs during the load test.
data_integrity_requirements: No workflow state corruption due to concurrency issues.

test_cases.test_name: Verification of EHR/LIMS Integration and Data Synchronization
test_cases.objective: Verify successful bidirectional data exchange and synchronization between the Orchestration Platform, EHR, and LIMS systems.
prerequisites: EHR, LIMS, and Courier systems are configured and accessible via defined APIs.
Test patient data (e.g., Apheresis Order) is staged in the EHR.
OIDC/SSO is functional for system access.

test_steps.action: Initiate a new patient journey workflow in the Orchestration Platform, triggering data pull from the EHR (e.g., patient demographics, order details).
test_steps.expected_result: The platform successfully ingests and validates the required patient data from the EHR without errors.
data_to_capture: API response codes for EHR pull

test_steps.action: Advance the workflow to the manufacturing slotting stage and simulate a successful LIMS notification for material allocation.
test_steps.expected_result: The platform receives the LIMS confirmation, updates the internal status, and logs the handoff event in the audit trail.
data_to_capture: Audit trail entry for LIMS confirmation

test_steps.action: Complete the workflow step requiring data submission back to the EHR (e.g., final release status).
test_steps.expected_result: The platform successfully pushes the final status update to the EHR via API, confirmed by EHR system logs.
data_to_capture: API response codes for EHR push
Verification of status change in EHR

acceptance_criteria: All required data elements are transferred accurately between the three systems.
Integration handoffs are fully recorded in the audit trail (URS-028-008).
data_integrity_requirements: Data mapping validation
Error handling for failed API calls

test_cases.test_name: Verification of Custom Algorithm Module Versioning and Decision Explainability
test_cases.objective: Verify that the system correctly loads and executes a specific version of a custom algorithm module and generates required explainability artifacts for its decision.
prerequisites: Two distinct, versioned custom algorithm modules (V1.0 and V1.1) are deployed in containers.
A test patient scenario is configured that requires the custom matching optimization (URS-028-006).
The system is configured to use V1.0 initially.

test_steps.action: Execute the workflow using the default configuration (V1.0) for a patient requiring optimization.
test_steps.expected_result: The platform executes the matching optimization using V1.0, and the resulting decision (e.g., Lot X assigned) is recorded.

test_steps.action: Retrieve the explainability artifact generated for the decision made in Step 1.
test_steps.expected_result: A detailed artifact is generated, clearly stating the inputs, the logic path taken by V1.0, and the resulting score/decision (URS-028-016).

test_steps.action: Update the system configuration to force the use of the newer custom module version (V1.1) and re-run the exact same patient scenario.
test_steps.expected_result: The platform successfully loads V1.1, executes the matching, and produces a potentially different, but valid, matching decision.

test_steps.action: Verify that the containerized module (URS-028-015) is correctly identified and isolated during execution.
test_steps.expected_result: System logs confirm that only the V1.1 container image was instantiated for the second run.

acceptance_criteria: The system correctly switches between deployed algorithm versions.
Explainability artifacts are generated for every decision made by a custom module.
data_integrity_requirements: Verification that the algorithm version used matches the configuration setting.

test_cases.test_name: Verify OIDC SSO and Scanner Identity Authentication
test_cases.objective: Verify that the system correctly enforces Single Sign-On (SSO) via OIDC and authenticates device identity for scanning operations.
prerequisites: OIDC provider configured and reachable.
Test user accounts provisioned.
Test scanners configured with valid device identities.

test_steps.action: Attempt to access the main orchestration dashboard using a standard user account without prior OIDC login.
test_steps.expected_result: User is successfully redirected to the OIDC login page and gains access upon successful authentication.

test_steps.action: Use a configured scanner to perform a Chain-of-Identity verification scan (e.g., patient wristband scan) without logging into the application interface first.
test_steps.expected_result: The scanner successfully authenticates via its device identity and records the scan event, linking it to the session context.
data_to_capture: Scan result and associated user/session context

test_steps.action: Attempt to perform a critical action (e.g., custody transfer) using a scanner whose device identity has been temporarily revoked or expired.
test_steps.expected_result: The system rejects the action, citing device authentication failure, and logs a security event.

acceptance_criteria: All user access is mediated successfully through OIDC.
Scanners authenticate successfully using their registered device identities.
Unauthorized access attempts via device identity failure are blocked and logged.
data_integrity_requirements: Ensure device identity is correctly linked to custody records.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Workflow Template Configuration and Customization Limits
test_cases.objective: Verify the ability to configure complex end-to-end workflow templates using vendor configuration tools and confirm the boundary conditions for customization.
prerequisites: System is fully installed and integrated.
Access to the workflow configuration interface.

test_steps.action: Configure a new, complex workflow template combining Apheresis, Manufacturing Slotting, QC Hold, and Infusion steps, utilizing standard vendor configuration options.
test_steps.expected_result: The workflow template is successfully saved, validated by the system, and appears ready for deployment.

test_steps.action: Deploy the configured template and initiate a test patient journey, ensuring all required custody handoffs (URS-028-002) are triggered.
test_steps.expected_result: The patient journey progresses through all configured stages, and custody events are logged correctly.
data_to_capture: Time taken for custody verification steps

test_steps.action: Attempt to configure a workflow step that requires logic exceeding the vendor scripting capabilities (e.g., complex external API call not supported by standard connectors), forcing the use of the custom module hook.
test_steps.expected_result: The system correctly flags the step as requiring a custom module integration or rejects the configuration if the hook is not properly defined.
data_to_capture: System response when attempting to bypass custom module requirement

acceptance_criteria: Complex workflows can be built entirely using vendor configuration tools.
All required handoffs within the configured workflow trigger appropriate custody/identity checks.
The system enforces the boundary between vendor configuration and required custom module implementation.
data_integrity_requirements: Verify that configuration changes do not corrupt existing active workflows.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Dual-Scanning CoC/CoI Enforcement During Handoff
test_cases.objective: To verify that the system strictly enforces dual-scanning verification for all critical custody and identity handoffs between workflow stages.
prerequisites: System configured with at least two distinct workflow stages requiring custody transfer (e.g., Apheresis to Quarantine).
Valid patient ID and corresponding material lot IDs available.
Two functional barcode scanners configured and linked to the system.

test_steps.action: Initiate a new patient journey workflow template.
test_steps.expected_result: The system advances to the first custody checkpoint (e.g., Apheresis completion).

test_steps.action: Attempt to confirm the custody transfer by scanning only the material lot ID once.
test_steps.expected_result: The system rejects the transfer, displaying an error requiring the second verification scan (e.g., patient ID scan or second operator confirmation).

test_steps.action: Perform the required dual-scan verification (Lot ID scan followed by Patient ID scan).
test_steps.expected_result: The system successfully records the custody handoff, timestamps the event, and advances the workflow to the next stage.

test_steps.action: Review the audit trail for the recorded handoff event.
test_steps.expected_result: The audit trail entry must explicitly show both successful scans, the identity of the operator performing the scans, and the successful transition.

acceptance_criteria: The system must prevent workflow progression unless two distinct, required identity/custody scans are successfully logged.
All successful handoffs must be immutably recorded in the audit trail.
data_integrity_requirements: Ensure no data loss or corruption during the custody event logging.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Exception Workflow Triggering and Data Capture for MES Handoff Failure
test_cases.objective: To verify that the system correctly triggers the configured exception workflow when a critical integration point (MES) fails to acknowledge a required data update.
prerequisites: Workflow configured to integrate with a simulated MES system.
A specific workflow step (e.g., Manufacturing Slotting) is configured to trigger an exception workflow upon MES communication failure.
The MES simulator is set to intentionally fail the next required API call.

test_steps.action: Advance a test patient journey to the step immediately preceding the MES integration point.
test_steps.expected_result: The system is ready to send the data payload to the MES.

test_steps.action: Trigger the workflow step, causing the simulated MES integration to return a defined failure response (e.g., 500 error).
test_steps.expected_result: The system does not advance the primary workflow but immediately initiates the pre-configured exception handling workflow.

test_steps.action: Verify the system's response within the exception workflow, specifically checking for the creation of a required notification/task for manual review.
test_steps.expected_result: A high-priority task is created, assigned to the appropriate user group, and the patient journey status is flagged as 'Hold - Integration Failure'.

test_steps.action: Review the audit trail and system logs related to the failure and exception trigger.
test_steps.expected_result: The audit trail clearly documents the integration failure, the system's decision to invoke the exception path, and the initiation of the manual review task.
data_to_capture: Audit Log Snippet for Exception Trigger

acceptance_criteria: The system must successfully intercept the integration failure and prevent data corruption or silent workflow stalling.
The configured exception workflow (URS-028-004) must be correctly invoked and generate actionable alerts/tasks.
data_integrity_requirements: Ensure the patient journey state is correctly paused and flagged to prevent downstream processing errors.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Configuration of Advanced Patient-to-Lot Matching Optimization
test_cases.objective: To verify that the system correctly utilizes the optional custom-developed algorithm module for patient-to-lot matching optimization based on configurable parameters.
prerequisites: System is fully deployed and configured.
Custom algorithm module (URS-028-006) is installed and versioned.
Test patient data and available manufacturing lots are loaded.

test_steps.action: Configure the workflow engine to utilize the custom matching algorithm module for a specific therapy type.
test_steps.expected_result: The system accepts the configuration change without error, indicating the module is active.

test_steps.action: Submit a new patient order requiring lot allocation, ensuring multiple viable lots exist.
test_steps.expected_result: The system processes the request and assigns the lot that yields the highest optimization score as determined by the custom algorithm.
data_to_capture: Optimization Score generated by the module

test_steps.action: Review the audit trail and explainability artifacts associated with the matching decision.
test_steps.expected_result: The audit trail records the decision, and the explainability artifact clearly details the inputs and the rationale derived from the custom algorithm.

acceptance_criteria: The custom matching module is successfully invoked.
The lot assignment aligns with the optimization logic defined in the module.
All decision steps are traceable via audit trail and explainability reports.
data_integrity_requirements: Ensure the custom module does not corrupt lot inventory data.

test_cases.test_name: Verify System Resilience Under Peak Load and Integration Latency
test_cases.objective: To verify that the system maintains required event processing latency (< 1 second) while orchestrating 1,000 concurrent patient journeys and handling external integration calls.
prerequisites: System is configured for 1,000 concurrent users/journeys.
All integrated systems (EHR, LIMS, MES) are available and responding.
Load testing tools are configured to simulate traffic.

test_steps.action: Initiate the load test simulating 1,000 concurrent patient journeys, ensuring each journey involves multiple state transitions requiring integration calls (e.g., LIMS sample registration).
test_steps.expected_result: All 1,000 journeys progress through the workflow stages without crashing or deadlocking.

test_steps.action: Monitor the processing latency for critical state transitions (e.g., custody handoff events) throughout the duration of the load test.
test_steps.expected_result: 99% of all recorded event processing latencies must be less than 1 second, as per URS-028-012.
data_to_capture: Number of events exceeding 1 second threshold

test_steps.action: Verify that the audit trail (URS-028-008) remains complete and accurate for a sample set of 50 transactions processed during peak load.
test_steps.expected_result: All sampled transactions have complete, time-stamped audit records reflecting the exact sequence of events.

acceptance_criteria: System successfully orchestrates 1,000 concurrent journeys.
Event processing latency remains below the 1-second threshold for the vast majority of transactions.
Data integrity (audit trail) is maintained under stress.
data_integrity_requirements: No data loss or corruption during high-volume transaction processing.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Configuration of Workflow Templates for All Stages
test_cases.objective: Verify that all required end-to-end workflow templates (apheresis, manufacturing, QC, infusion) can be configured using vendor tools and are correctly linked.
prerequisites: System is fully installed and configured.
Access to workflow configuration module with administrative rights.
Defined configuration parameters for at least one end-to-end patient journey.

test_steps.action: Access the workflow configuration interface and create a new template named 'Full_CGT_Journey_Test'.
test_steps.expected_result: The system successfully creates the new template shell.

test_steps.action: Configure the Apheresis stage within the template, setting mandatory fields and defining the handoff trigger to the Manufacturing stage.
test_steps.expected_result: The Apheresis stage configuration is saved without errors, and the handoff logic is validated by the system.

test_steps.action: Configure the Manufacturing, QC Release, and Infusion stages sequentially, ensuring all required steps (including e-signature prompts) are present.
test_steps.expected_result: The complete end-to-end workflow template is successfully built and marked as 'Ready for Deployment'.

test_steps.action: Deploy the configured template and initiate a test patient journey using this template.
test_steps.expected_result: The test patient journey successfully progresses through the initial Apheresis step, triggering the expected data transfer for the next stage.

acceptance_criteria: All four required workflow stages (Apheresis, Manufacturing, QC, Infusion) are successfully configured within a single template.
The system correctly validates the sequence and mandatory data requirements for each stage transition.
data_integrity_requirements: Ensure no data loss occurs during the simulated stage handoffs.

test_cases.test_name: Verify System Response to Simultaneous Integration Failures
test_cases.objective: Verify the system's ability to handle and log exceptions when multiple critical external integrations (EHR, LIMS) fail simultaneously during a high-volume process.
prerequisites: System is operational and running under simulated high load (URS-028-011).
Integration endpoints for EHR and LIMS are configured to return simulated failure responses (e.g., 500 errors or timeouts).
Exception handling workflows (URS-028-004) are configured to capture these failures.

test_steps.action: Initiate 50 concurrent patient journeys that require immediate data exchange with both EHR and LIMS systems (e.g., initial patient registration and material request).
test_steps.expected_result: The system attempts to communicate with both external systems for all 50 journeys.

test_steps.action: Monitor the system logs and the dedicated exception dashboard while the external systems return failure responses.
test_steps.expected_result: The system successfully captures the integration failures, places the affected journeys into the designated exception queue, and does not crash or hang.

test_steps.action: Verify that the audit trail (URS-028-008) accurately records the failure event, including the external system involved and the timestamp.
test_steps.expected_result: Audit trail entries confirm the exact nature and timing of the integration failures for all 50 transactions.
data_to_capture: Sample Audit Trail Entries for 5 transactions

test_steps.action: Restore the EHR and LIMS integration endpoints to normal operation and verify that the exception workflows correctly attempt reprocessing or allow manual intervention.
test_steps.expected_result: Affected journeys are either automatically resumed or flagged clearly for manual review as per exception workflow configuration.

acceptance_criteria: The platform remains stable and responsive despite simultaneous integration failures.
All integration failures are logged accurately in the audit trail.
Affected workflows are correctly routed to the defined exception handling mechanism (URS-028-004).
data_integrity_requirements: Ensure that no partial data updates are committed to the system database during the failure/recovery cycle.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Configuration of Risk Scoring Rules and Vendor Scripting
test_cases.objective: Verify that the system correctly applies and enforces complex, configurable risk scoring rules defined via vendor scripting capabilities.
prerequisites: System is fully configured and operational.
Access to administrative interface for rule configuration.
Test patient data sets representing low, medium, and high-risk profiles.

test_steps.action: Configure a new vendor script rule that assigns a 'High Risk' score if the patient's age > 65 AND the planned apheresis date is within 7 days of the manufacturing slot allocation.
test_steps.expected_result: The system accepts and saves the new vendor script rule without errors.

test_steps.action: Process a test patient record matching the 'High Risk' criteria (Age=70, Apheresis Date=T+5 days) through the orchestration workflow.
test_steps.expected_result: The workflow automatically flags the patient journey as 'High Risk' and triggers the defined escalation workflow (e.g., requiring manual review before QC release).

test_steps.action: Process a test patient record matching only one criterion (Age=70, but Apheresis Date=T+10 days) and verify the resulting score.
test_steps.expected_result: The system calculates a score below the 'High Risk' threshold (e.g., Medium or Low), allowing standard progression.
data_to_capture: Calculated risk score for the second patient

acceptance_criteria: Configurable risk scoring rules based on vendor scripting are correctly interpreted by the engine.
Risk scores accurately reflect the defined logic for all test cases.
The system correctly triggers subsequent workflow steps based on the calculated risk score.
regulatory_basis: URS-028-005 (Support configurable risk scoring rules using vendor scripting).
data_integrity_requirements: Ensure risk score calculation is immutable and logged in the audit trail.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Containerization and Versioning of Custom Algorithm Modules
test_cases.objective: Verify that optional custom-developed algorithm modules are deployed as versioned containers and that the orchestration platform correctly selects and utilizes the specified version.
prerequisites: System supports containerized module deployment (e.g., Docker/Kubernetes integration).
Two distinct versions (V1.0 and V1.1) of a custom patient-to-lot matching module are available in the repository.

test_steps.action: Configure the orchestration platform to utilize Custom Module V1.0 for the patient-to-lot matching step in Workflow Template A.
test_steps.expected_result: The system successfully registers and links V1.0 to Workflow Template A.
data_to_capture: Module version linked to Template A

test_steps.action: Execute a patient journey using Workflow Template A and confirm that the matching decision artifact references Module V1.0.
test_steps.expected_result: The decision artifact explicitly states that the matching logic was executed by Module V1.0.

test_steps.action: Update the configuration to switch Workflow Template A to use Custom Module V1.1, ensuring V1.0 remains available but inactive.
test_steps.expected_result: The system successfully deploys and links V1.1 without disrupting existing active workflows using V1.0.
data_to_capture: Module version linked to Template A post-update

test_steps.action: Execute a new patient journey using the updated Workflow Template A and verify the matching decision artifact references Module V1.1.
test_steps.expected_result: The new journey utilizes the logic from V1.1, and the explainability artifact confirms this version.
data_to_capture: Explainability artifact output for V1.1 execution

acceptance_criteria: Custom modules are deployed and managed as versioned containers.
The orchestration platform correctly selects the configured module version for execution.
Explainability artifacts clearly identify the version of the custom module used for the decision.
regulatory_basis: URS-028-006 (Allow optional custom-developed modules for patient-to-lot matching optimization).
URS-028-015 (Custom algorithm modules shall be containerized and versioned).
URS-028-016 (Provide explainability artifacts for algorithm decisions).
data_integrity_requirements: Ensure that module versioning prevents accidental execution of unvalidated or older versions in critical paths.
